messages:
Maya: Ugh—fiber dropped at 9:07am and the baby decided my coffee should be a keyboard accessory. Hotspot tethered to the rescue. Photo: https://i.imgur.com/placeholder.jpg
Ethan: oh no 😂 pics pls
Maya: https://i.imgur.com/placeholder.jpg
Maya: Also FYI hotspot was surprisingly stable on T-Mobile. Anyone got tips to keep it rock-solid during calls?
Devon: Try forcing 5GHz on the phone's hotspot if available, less interference. Also put the phone on a small elevation so it gets a better signal.
Lina: On Mac, USB tethering is way more stable than wifi hotspot. Settings > Personal Hotspot > Connect via USB. Mac picks it up as a network device.
Sam: If you need persistent backup, cheap LTE travel routers (TP-Link M7xxx series) are great. Plug in battery or USB-C and it acts like a regular router. < $120.
Maya: Will try USB tethering next time. Also re-routed the desk cables and zip-tied the power strip under the desk (no more spaghetti). Photo: https://i.imgur.com/deskjpg.jpg
Ethan: we should do a "WFH Desk tour" thread Friday — poll? :raised_hands:
ops-bot: Reminder: if you log an ISP outage please include a quick reachability test: `ping 8.8.8.8 -c 50` and attach the output.
Lina: Also, baby-safe travel mugs from @Sam's rec worked great btw :heart:
Maya: Thanks all — hotspot + some cable ducting = saved my meeting. ISP scheduled repair for tomorrow morning. Back to calls (with phone propped on a cereal box).
